chunks: And what Al-Saffar narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Musa Al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalloob from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:
"Whoever of the men separates himself from his family behind a door or lowers a curtain, then the dowry (mahr) has become obligatory upon him."

So these two reports do not contradict what we have previously mentioned from the reports, because these two reports are to be understood as referring to the case where the man and the woman are both suspected (muttahaman) after their seclusion, and he denies the sexual intercourse; then if the matter is thus, they are not believed in their statements, and the man is obliged to pay the full dowry, and the woman must observe the waiting period (iddah).
And if they are truthful, or if there is a way by which their truthfulness can be known, then the intercourse alone obligates the dowry.
And that which indicates that when they are suspected, the ruling regarding it is what we mentioned, is what was narrated:

key_terms.أَجَافَ: To separate or turn away, here implying physical separation or privacy
key_terms.الْعِدَّةَ: The waiting period for a woman

ai.seo_question: When is the full dowry obligatory upon a husband if he denies consummation of marriage?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this narration from Ja'far al-Sadiq within the jurisprudence of *khalwah* (marital seclusion), explaining that the obligation of the full dowry (*mahr*) arises presumptively when both spouses are considered *muttahaman* (suspected) of intercourse yet the husband denies it. This ruling balances evidentiary standards, noting that the full dowry is not automatically enforced if their truthfulness can be verified or if a clear path to proof exists, thereby preventing unjust financial liability.
